studies.title: Dietary glutathione supplementation enhances antioxidant activity and protects against lipopolysaccharide-induced acute hepatopancreatic injury and cell apoptos
studies.abstract: Eriocheir sinensis (E. sinensis) is an important aquaculture species in China. However, deteriorating water environments lead to oxidative stress in these crabs, which subsequently reduces their quality and yield. Glutathione (GSH) is an endogenous antioxidant that is used to mitigate oxidative stress. However, whether dietary GSH can enhance the resistance of E. sinensis to oxidative stress remains unclear. Herein, crabs were fed dietary GSH (the basal diet was supplemented with 0, 300, 600, 900, and 1200 mg/kg diet weight of GSH) for up to 3 weeks and, then, challenged with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 400 μg/kg body weight). After 6 h, their hepatopancreas were sampled. Diet supplementation with 600 and 900 mg/kg diet weight GSH not only increased the content of GSH in the hepatopancreas, but also enhanced the activities and mRNA expressions of superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px), and glutathione-S-transferase (GST) (P < 0.05), compared to that in control crabs challenged with LPS alone. Diet supplementation with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH also significantly increased the enzyme activities of GSH reductase and γ-glutamyl cysteine synthetase (γ-GCS) in LPS-treated crabs. Haematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, electron microscopy, and flow cytometry were used to examine the structure and subcellular structure of and apoptosis in the hepatopancreas. The histopathology and sub-microstructure analysis results also showed that diet supplementation with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH significantly alleviated damage in crabs challenged with LPS and decreased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and cell apoptosis ratios in the hepatopancreas, compared to the LPS-treated crabs. To further understand the effect of dietary GSH on LPS-induced apoptosis, the activities and gene or protein expressions of apoptosis-related factors were evaluated. As a result, diet supplementation with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH significantly decreased the activities of caspases-3, -8, and -9 and inhibited the relative expression of caspase-3 and -8 but increased the expression of B-cell lymphoma-2 (bcl-2) and B-cell lymphoma-2-associated X inhibitor (bax inhibitor) in crabs challenged with LPS. This treatment further significantly downregulated the relative protein levels of caspase-3, -8, -9 and Bax and upregulated those of Bcl-2 in crabs challenged with LPS. However, treatment with 1200 mg/kg GSH caused the opposite effects. Overall, our results reveal that appropriate diets supplemented with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH could enhance the antioxidant capacity and anti-apoptotic mechanisms in crabs after LPS injection, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the application of dietary GSH in E. sinensis.

studies.title: Effect of long-term oral glutathione supplementation on gut microbiome of type 2 diabetic individuals.
studies.abstract: The aim of this study was to check the effect of long-term oral glutathione (GSH) supplementation on alteration in gut microbiome of Indian diabetic individuals. Early morning fresh stool sample of diabetic individuals recruited in a randomized clinical trial wherein they were given 500 mg GSH supplementation orally once a day for a period of 6 months was collected and gut microbiome was analysed using high throughput 16S rRNA metagenomic sequencing. Long-term GSH supplementation as reported in our earlier work showed significant increase in body stores of GSH and stabilized decreased glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c). Analysis of gut microbiome revealed that abundance of phylum Proteobacteria significantly decreased (P < 0.05) in individuals with GSH supplementation after 6 months compared to those without it. Beneficial dominant genera such as Megasphaera, Bacteroides, and Megamonas were found to be significantly enriched (P < 0.05), while pathogenic Escherichia/Shigella was found to be depleted (P < 0.05) after supplementation. Data clearly demonstrate that GSH supplementation along with antidiabetic treatment helps restore the gut microbiome by enriching beneficial bacteria of healthy gut and reducing significantly the load of pathogenic bacteria of diabetic gut.

studies.title: l-Cysteine and Vitamin D Co-Supplementation Alleviates Markers of Musculoskeletal Disorders in Vitamin D-Deficient High-Fat Diet-Fed Mice.
studies.abstract: Vitamin D (VD) deficiency is associated with musculoskeletal disorders. This study examines whether co-supplementation of l-cysteine (LC) and VD is better than monotherapy with LC or VD at alleviating musculoskeletal dyshomeostasis in the skeletal muscle of VD-deficient high-fat diet (HFD-VD-) fed mice. Mice were fed a healthy diet or an HFD; for VD-deficient animals, the mice were maintained on a HFD-VD-diet (16 weeks); after the first 8 weeks, the HFD-VD-diet-fed mice were supplemented for another 8 weeks with LC, VD-alone, or the same doses of LC + VD by oral gavage. Saline and olive oil served as controls. Myotubes were exposed with high-glucose, palmitate, Monocyte Chemoattractant Protein 1 (MCP-1), and Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF), to mimic the in vivo microenvironment. In vitro deficiencies of glutathione and hydrogen sulfide were induced by knockdown of GCLC and CSE genes. Relative gene expression of biomarkers (myogenic: MyoD, Mef2c, Csrp3; muscle dystrophy: Atrogin1, Murf1, and Myostatin; bone modeling and remodeling: RANK, RANKL, OPG) were analyzed using qRT-PCR. Co-supplementatoin with LC + VD showed beneficial effects on gene expression of myogenic markers and OPG but reduced markers of dystrophy, RANK/RANKL in comparison to LC or VD alone-supplementation. In vitro myotubes treated with glutathione (GSH) precursors also showed a positive effect on OPG and the myogenesis genes, and inhibited RANK/RANKL and muscle-dystrophy markers. This study reveals that the co-supplementation of LC with VD significantly alleviates the markers of musculoskeletal disorders in the skeletal muscle better than monotherapy with LC or VD in HFD-VD-fed mice.

studies.title: Reduced glutathione supplementation in practical diet improves the growth, anti-oxidative capacity, disease resistance and gut morphology of shrimp Litopenaeus
studies.abstract: The present study was conducted to investigate the effects of reduced glutathione (GSH) supplementation in practical diet on growth performance, anti-oxidative response, disease resistance and intestine morphology of shrimp Litopenaeus vannamei. Two control diets based on the commercial formulation were designed with high level (27%) and low level (22%) of fish meal, respectively. Based on the control diet with low level of fish meal, 75, 150 and 225 mg/kg of GSH were added, respectively, to make the other three experimental diets. The five formulated diets were named as C1, C2, G1, G2 and G3, respectively. The shrimp (initial body weight: 0.30 ± 0.02 g) were fed with the five experimental diets for 8 weeks followed by a challenge test with Vibrio parahaemolyticus. The results showed that the specific growth rate (SGR) of shrimp in the C2 group was significantly lower than that in C1. The SGRs in G1 and G2 had no significant difference with those in C1 and C2. However, the SGR in G3 was significantly lower than that in C1. The serum GSH concentration in C2 was significantly lower than the other groups, but the malondialdehyde concentration was significantly higher. The supplementation of dietary GSH significantly improved the total anti-oxidative capacity and activities of glutathione S-transferase and glutathione peroxidase in serum. The villus height of intestine in the GSH supplemented groups had no significant difference with C1, but was significantly higher than C2. The jejunum wall thickness of intestine in G2 and G3 was significantly higher than those in the other groups. After the challenge test, the cumulative mortalities in G1 and G2 were significantly lower than C1 and C2. However, there was no significant difference in cumulative mortalities among G3, C1 and C2. In conclusion, based on the present experimental conditions, 75-150 mg/kg of GSH was suggested to be supplemented into the practical diet to improve the growth, anti-oxidative capacity, disease resistance and gut health of shrimp L. vannamei.

studies.title: Glutathione in Skin Aging and Tissue Regeneration: A Systematic Review of Molecular Mechanisms, Redox Modulation, and Biomedical Implications.
studies.abstract: Glutathione (GSH) is a central regulator of redox homeostasis, melanogenesis, and cellular repair, and has gained increasing attention in dermatology for its potential roles in skin brightening, anti-aging, and tissue regeneration. This systematic review evaluated molecular, clinical, and translational evidence of glutathione's applications and safety across different delivery modalities. The review followed PRISMA guidelines and included studies published between 2000 and 2025. A total of 194 studies met the inclusion criteria, evaluating the effectiveness of glutathione in esthetic dermatology and regenerative medicine. Topical and oral glutathione demonstrated favorable effects on pigmentation, skin brightness, hydration, and oxidative stress markers. Injectable glutathione increases systemic levels rapidly, but is associated with short-lasting effects and potential safety concerns. Glutathione S-transferases facilitate the conjugation of glutathione to electrophilic xenobiotics, thereby protecting proteins and nucleic acids from electrophile-induced damage. Glutathione Peroxidase employs GSH as an electron donor to reduce hydrogen peroxide and lipid hydroperoxides, thus protecting membrane lipids, mitochondrial membranes, and DNA from oxidative damage. Glutathione facilitates the regeneration of other antioxidants, such as vitamin C and vitamin E, through redox cycling. A consistent correlation exists between reduced GSH levels and neuronal dysfunction. Elevated GSH levels enhance cellular resistance to oxidative stress and reduce apoptotic signaling. GSH plays a pivotal role in cutaneous aging and tissue repair through redox regulation, mitochondrial protection, and the modulation of inflammatory and extracellular matrix pathways. To elucidate the clinical significance of glutathione, future research should focus on conducting randomized controlled trials, developing standardized formulations, and performing long-term safety assessments.

studies.title: Formulation-dependent differences in systemic glutathione availability: Comparative pharmacokinetics of orally dissolving film and tablet formulations in health
studies.abstract:
Background

Glutathione is a tripeptide involved in antioxidant defense; however, its systemic availability following oral administration remains controversial, and pharmacokinetic differences between formulations in humans are not well characterized.

Objective

This study compared the pharmacokinetics and short-term supplementation effects of an orally dissolving film (ODF) and a conventional tablet formulation of glutathione in healthy adults.

Methods

In Study I, a randomized open-label crossover trial evaluated single-dose (300 mg) pharmacokinetics following administration of ODF or tablets. In Study II, participants consumed ODF (100 mg/day) or tablets (100 mg/day) for 4 weeks.

Results

Plasma glutathione concentrations were higher in the ODF group, with significant differences at 4 and 6 h. The ODF formulation showed a longer Tmax and tended toward higher Cmax and systemic exposure (iAUC0-6h). During 4-week supplementation, both formulations increased circulating glutathione levels, with no significant changes in oxidative stress-related biomarkers. No adverse events were reported.

Conclusions

The ODF formulation exhibited a distinct pharmacokinetic profile and showed a trend toward greater systemic glutathione exposure compared with the tablet formulation. These findings suggest that formulation characteristics may contribute to differences in the bioavailability and pharmacokinetic behavior of orally administered glutathione.

Clinical trial registration

Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS), KCT0011710.

studies.title: Randomized controlled trial of oral glutathione supplementation on body stores of glutathione.
studies.abstract: Glutathione (GSH), the most abundant endogenous antioxidant, is a critical regulator of oxidative stress and immune function. While oral GSH has been shown to be bioavailable in laboratory animal models, its efficacy in humans has not been established. Our objective was to determine the long-term effectiveness of oral GSH supplementation on body stores of GSH in healthy adults. A 6-month randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial of oral GSH (250 or 1,000 mg/day) on GSH levels in blood, erythrocytes, plasma, lymphocytes and exfoliated buccal mucosal cells was conducted in 54 non-smoking adults. Secondary outcomes on a subset of subjects included a battery of immune markers. GSH levels in blood increased after 1, 3 and 6 months versus baseline at both doses. At 6 months, mean GSH levels increased 30-35 % in erythrocytes, plasma and lymphocytes and 260 % in buccal cells in the high-dose group (P < 0.05). GSH levels increased 17 and 29 % in blood and erythrocytes, respectively, in the low-dose group (P < 0.05). In most cases, the increases were dose and time dependent, and levels returned to baseline after a 1-month washout period. A reduction in oxidative stress in both GSH dose groups was indicated by decreases in the oxidized to reduced glutathione ratio in whole blood after 6 months. Natural killer cytotoxicity increased >twofold in the high-dose group versus placebo (P < 0.05) at 3 months. These findings show, for the first time, that daily consumption of GSH supplements was effective at increasing body compartment stores of GSH.

studies.title: Nrp1 Signaling Reprograms Glutathione Metabolism to Drive Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Severe Asthma.
studies.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction drives persistent inflammation in severe asthma, yet its upstream metabolic regulation remains unclear. Induced sputum from patients with severe asthma was analyzed and integrated with transcriptomic datasets from independent cohorts. Two mouse models (C57BL/6J) were used for in vivo validation with multi-omics profiling, and mechanistic studies were performed in air-liquid interface-cultured primary human airway epithelial cells. Glutathione reduced form (GSHr) was markedly depleted in sputum and associated with poor disease control and mixed granulocytic inflammation in patients with severe asthma. Multi-omics analyses revealed coordinated disruption of glutathione (GSH) metabolism, including oxidized GSH accumulation, reduced synthesis and glutathione-S-transferase activity, and impaired mitochondrial GSH transport. GSH supplementation alleviated airway inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas pharmacological inhibition of GST exacerbated these effects. Mitochondrial analyses identified suppressed SLC25A39 expression as a key mediator of defective GSH transport and redox imbalance. Transcriptomic profiling of airway biopsies showed upregulation of Neuropilin-1 (Nrp1), closely associated with altered glutathione pathways. Targeting the Nrp1 b1 domain restored mitochondrial GSH metabolism and attenuated airway inflammation. These findings identify an Nrp-centered metabolic pathway that disrupts mitochondrial homeostasis and drives inflammatory amplification, highlighting mitochondria-targeted therapeutic strategies for severe asthma.

studies.title: The effect of reduced L-glutathione supplementation on TNF-α, hs-CRP, and neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio in maintenance hemodialysis patients.
studies.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the main cause of mortality in patients with chronic kidney disease stage 5 on dialysis (CKD-5D). High sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) are several inflammatory parameters associated with high cardiovascular events in CKD-5D. The main aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of reduced L-glutathione supplementation on serum hs-CRP, TNF-α, and NLR in patients with CKD-5D. This study is a quasi-experimental research with one group pretest-posttest design. Subjects included were patients with CKD-5D who routinely underwent hemodialysis therapy two times a week in Hasan Sadikin General Hospital. Serum hs-CRP, TNF-α, and NLR levels were obtained before and after the intervention of reduced L-glutathione supplementation dosing of one thousand milligrams a day for four weeks. Statistical analysis was then conducted using the Wilcoxon test. There were 26 hemodialysis patients included in the study, with a median age of 43 years and a male predominance. There was a significant decrease in serum TNF-α level after reduced L-glutathione supplementation for 4 weeks, 5.40 (-10.80-0.00) pg/mL, p = 0.002. However, there was no statistically significant decrease in either serum hs-CRP level, 0.40 (-0.70-0.80) mg/L (p = 0.656), or NLR with a difference of 0.55 (0.30-1.00) p = 0.055. Exogenous oral reduced glutathione supplementation for four weeks significantly reduced TNF-α level, but no significant decrease in hs-CRP level and NLR in patients with CKD-5D.

studies.title: Glutathione Primes Mitochondrial Autophagy to Guide Pulp-Dentine Complex Repair.
studies.abstract:
Aim

Pulp-dentine complex repair following injury is fundamental to preserving tooth vitality and function. Despite advances in understanding reparative dentinogenesis, the molecular mechanisms orchestrating odontogenic differentiation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) remain fragmented, lacking systematic integration across transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic levels. This study employs integrated multi-omics approaches to identify key regulatory pathways during odontogenic differentiation and elucidate the underlying mechanisms controlling pulp-dentine complex repair.

Methodology

Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on human carious and healthy pulp tissues. Temporal proteomic and metabolomic profiling was conducted during hDPSCs' odontogenic differentiation. Based on multi-omics integration revealing glutathione metabolism as a central regulatory node, hDPSCs were treated with L-buthionine-sulfoximine (BSO) or exogenous glutathione (GSH). Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), GSH levels, mitochondrial membrane potential and mitophagy markers (PINK1/Parkin) were quantified. siRNA-mediated PINK1 knockdown was performed to assess the involvement of PINK1 in GSH-regulated odontogenic differentiation. A mouse molar injury model evaluated GSH effects on tertiary dentine formation in vivo.

Results

Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of oxidative stress response pathways in mesenchymal stem cells from injured pulp. Multi-omics integration identified glutathione metabolism as a central regulatory pathway, with glutamate-cysteine ligase catalytic subunit (GCLC) progressively upregulated during differentiation. BSO treatment depleted intracellular GSH, elevated ROS levels, suppressed PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and impaired odontogenic differentiation. GSH supplementation restored mitophagy activity and rescued differentiation capacity in vitro. PINK1 depletion impaired odontogenic differentiation and markedly attenuated the pro-differentiation effects of exogenous GSH. In vivo, GSH administration enhanced tertiary dentine formation and activated mitophagy pathways in injured dental pulp.

Conclusions

Our findings establish that the GCLC-mediated GSH antioxidant system orchestrates the odontogenic differentiation of dental pulp cells and pulp-dentine complex repair via the PINK1/Parkin-mitophagy axis, revealing a novel metabolic-oxideative signalling circuit as a potential therapeutic target for regenerative endodontics.

studies.title: Glutathione Impacts Both Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis Virulence and Amphibian Cellular Defense in a Chytridiomycosis Model.
studies.abstract: Glutathione has important roles in diverse infections, yet its involvement in the interaction between the deadly fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) and its amphibian hosts is still unclear. Using in vitro assays and a cell infection model, we examined how glutathione influences Bd virulence traits and cellular host disease resistance. For Bd, inhibition of glutathione reductase rapidly killed zoospores, indicating that glutathione is essential for this pathogen. In addition, exposure to exogenous glutathione promoted the potential for virulence through accelerated and increased zoospore release. In host amphibian cells, Bd infection decreased intracellular glutathione content and increased reactive oxygen species, suggesting that chytridiomycosis pathogenesis involves oxidative stress. Depletion of host glutathione before exposure to Bd increased infection severity, whereas amphibian cells with slightly elevated glutathione levels were partially protected against Bd. However, manipulation of host glutathione levels after the establishment of Bd infection did not impact its intracellular growth, implying that the host glutathione-mediated resistance only occurs during the initial Bd invasion process. Importantly, this effect of glutathione on host resistance is not a general response to pathogens, as it was not observed in cells exposed to the viral pathogen FV3. As glutathione increased both infectious zoospore production and host resistance to zoospore infection, our study suggests that this antioxidant may play an important role in the host/pathogen interaction during chytridiomycosis. Thus, environmental conditions and therapeutic approaches that affect glutathione systems in the host and/or pathogen have the potential to alter chytridiomycosis dynamics and should be further explored.

studies.title: Glutathione as a Potential Neuroprotectant Against MDMA-Induced Oxidative Stress, Neuroinflammation, and Apoptosis in the Rat Brain.
studies.abstract: 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), widely misused for its euphoric and stimulant properties, induces overt neurotoxicity in rodents and non-human primates and is associated with profound neurochemical and structural brain alterations. Its deleterious effects are primarily mediated through oxidative stress, neuroinflammatory responses, and apoptotic pathways. Glutathione, a crucial endogenous antioxidant, has been proposed as a potential neuroprotective agent capable of mitigating MDMA-induced cerebral damage.Sixty adult male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to six experimental groups and administered oral treatments for 56 days: MDMA (5 mg/kg or 15 mg/kg), glutathione (15 mg/kg), or their combinations. After treatment, brain tissues were harvested and evaluated for oxidative stress biomarkers (8-OHdG, MDA, GPx, GSH, GST, SOD), pro-inflammatory cytokines (MPO, NF-κB, TNF-α), ion transport enzymes (Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase, Ca²⁺ ATPase), neurotransmitter levels (dopamine, serotonin, AChE), and the apoptotic marker caspase-3. Histological analysis of the hippocampus was conducted to assess structural integrity. MDMA administration led to significant elevations in MDA and 8-OHdG, reductions in antioxidant enzymes (GPx, GST, GSH, SOD), upregulation of inflammatory mediators (MPO, NF-κB, TNF-α), and disruption of ion homeostasis via altered Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase and Ca²⁺ ATPase activities. Neurotransmitter imbalances were observed, characterized by increased AChE and serotonin levels and decreased dopamine. Caspase-3 activity was markedly elevated, indicating enhanced apoptosis. Co-administration of glutathione at low MDMA doses ameliorated these effects, restoring antioxidant defenses, suppressing inflammation, and preserving hippocampal architecture. However, its protective efficacy was notably diminished at higher MDMA concentrations. Glutathione confers partial neuroprotection against MDMA-induced neurotoxicity, particularly under moderate exposure conditions. Its antioxidative capacity contributes to the restoration of redox equilibrium and cellular integrity. Nonetheless, under high-dose MDMA exposure, the therapeutic potential of glutathione is limited, suggesting the necessity for complementary interventions targeting excitotoxicity and mitochondrial dysfunction.

This study aimed to determine whether supplementation with glutathione (GSH) and/or selenium (Se), as antioxidants, attenuates diethylnitrosamine (DEN)-induced hepatocarcinogenesis in mice. C57BL/6J male mice were randomly assigned to control, DEN, DEN + GSH, DEN + Se, and DEN + GSH + Se groups for 20 weeks. Daily supplementation with GSH and/or Se commenced in the first experimental week and continued throughout the study. DEN was administered in weeks 2-9 and 16-19 of the experimental period. studies.abstract: Intracellular levels of glutathione, the major mammalian antioxidant, are reported to decline with age in several species. To understand whether ageing affects circulating glutathione levels in cats, blood was sampled from two age groups, < 3 years and > 9 years. Further, to determine whether dietary supplementation with glutathione precursor glycine (GLY) affects glutathione concentrations in senior cats (> 8 years), a series of free GLY inclusion level dry diets were fed. Subsequently, a 16-week GLY feeding study was conducted in senior cats (> 7 years), measuring glutathione, and markers of oxidative stress. studies.title: Dietary glutathione supplementation attenuates oxidative stress and improves intestinal barrier in diquat-treated weaned piglets.
studies.abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the protective effects of glutathione (GSH) against oxidative stress and intestinal barrier disruption caused by diquat (an oxidative stress inducer) in weaned piglets. Twenty-four piglets were randomly assigned to four treatments with six pigs per treatment for an 18-d trial. Treatments were basal diet, basal diet + diquat challenge, 50 mg/kg GSH diets + diquat challenge and 100 mg/kg GSH diets + diquat challenge. On day 15, piglets in basal diet group and diquat-challenged groups were intraperitoneally injected with sterile saline and diquat at 10 mg/kg body weight, respectively. studies.title: Dietary glutathione supplementation enhances antioxidant activity and protects against lipopolysaccharide-induced acute hepatopancreatic injury and cell apoptos
studies.abstract: Eriocheir sinensis (E. sinensis) is an important aquaculture species in China. However, deteriorating water environments lead to oxidative stress in these crabs, which subsequently reduces their quality and yield. Glutathione (GSH) is an endogenous antioxidant that is used to mitigate oxidative stress. However, whether dietary GSH can enhance the resistance of E. sinensis to oxidative stress remains unclear. Herein, crabs were fed dietary GSH (the basal diet was supplemented with 0, 300, 600, 900, and 1200 mg/kg diet weight of GSH) for up to 3 weeks and, then, challenged with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 400 μg/kg body weight). After 6 h, their hepatopancreas were sampled. Diet supplementation with 600 and 900 mg/kg diet weight GSH not only increased the content of GSH in the hepatopancreas, but also enhanced the activities and mRNA expressions of superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px), and glutathione-S-transferase (GST) (P < 0.05), compared to that in control crabs challenged with LPS alone. Diet supplementation with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH also significantly increased the enzyme activities of GSH reductase and γ-glutamyl cysteine synthetase (γ-GCS) in LPS-treated crabs. Haematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, electron microscopy, and flow cytometry were used to examine the structure and subcellular structure of and apoptosis in the hepatopancreas. The histopathology and sub-microstructure analysis results also showed that diet supplementation with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH significantly alleviated damage in crabs challenged with LPS and decreased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and cell apoptosis ratios in the hepatopancreas, compared to the LPS-treated crabs. To further understand the effect of dietary GSH on LPS-induced apoptosis, the activities and gene or protein expressions of apoptosis-related factors were evaluated. As a result, diet supplementation with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH significantly decreased the activities of caspases-3, -8, and -9 and inhibited the relative expression of caspase-3 and -8 but increased the expression of B-cell lymphoma-2 (bcl-2) and B-cell lymphoma-2-associated X inhibitor (bax inhibitor) in crabs challenged with LPS. This treatment further significantly downregulated the relative protein levels of caspase-3, -8, -9 and Bax and upregulated those of Bcl-2 in crabs challenged with LPS. However, treatment with 1200 mg/kg GSH caused the opposite effects. Overall, our results reveal that appropriate diets supplemented with 600 or 900 mg/kg GSH could enhance the antioxidant capacity and anti-apoptotic mechanisms in crabs after LPS injection, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the application of dietary GSH in E. sinensis.

studies.title: Glutathione Supplementation of Parenteral Nutrition Prevents Oxidative Stress and Sustains Protein Synthesis in Guinea Pig Model.
studies.abstract: Peroxides contaminating parenteral nutrition (PN) limit the use of methionine as a precursor of cysteine. Thus, PN causes a cysteine deficiency, characterized by low levels of glutathione, the main molecule used in peroxide detoxification, and limited growth in individuals receiving long-term PN compared to the average population. We hypothesize that glutathione supplementation in PN can be used as a pro-cysteine that improves glutathione levels and protein synthesis and reduces oxidative stress caused by PN. One-month-old guinea pigs (7-8 per group) were used to compare glutathione-enriched to a non-enriched PN, animals on enteral nutrition were used as a reference. PN: Dextrose, amino acids (Primene), lipid emulsion (Intralipid), multivitamins, electrolytes; five-day infusion. Glutathione (GSH, GSSG, redox potential) and the incorporation of radioactive leucine into the protein fraction (protein synthesis index) were measured in the blood, lungs, liver, and gastrocnemius muscle. Data were analysed by ANOVA;

studies.title: Oral glutathione supplementation drastically reduces Helicobacter-induced gastric pathologies.
studies.abstract: Helicobacter (H.) suis causes gastric pathologies in both pigs and humans. Very little is known on the metabolism of this bacterium and its impact on the host. In this study, we have revealed the importance of the glutamate-generating metabolism, as shown by a complete depletion of glutamine (Gln) in the medium during H. suis culture. Besides Gln, H. suis can also convert glutathione (GSH) to glutamate, and both reactions are catalyzed by the H. suis γ-glutamyltranspeptidase (GGT). Both for H. pylori and H. suis, it has been hypothesized that the degradation of Gln and GSH may lead to a deficiency for the host, possibly initiating or promoting several pathologies. Therefore the in vivo effect of oral supplementation with Gln and GSH was assessed. Oral supplementation with Gln was shown to temper H. suis induced gastritis and epithelial (hyper)proliferation in Mongolian gerbils. Astonishingly, supplementation of the feed with GSH, another GGT substrate, resulted in inflammation and epithelial proliferation levels returning to baseline levels of uninfected controls. This indicates that Gln and GSH supplementation may help reducing tissue damage caused by Helicobacter infection in both humans and pigs, highlighting their potential as a supportive therapy during and after Helicobacter eradication therapy.

studies.title: Genomic analysis of an Arctic marine Tenacibaculum sp. SM2510 reveals its genetic potential for glutathione utilization.
studies.abstract: Glutathione is a key intracellular antioxidant, playing a crucial role in resisting oxidative stress and maintaining cellular redox homeostasis. However, the glutathione metabolic capacity of Tenacibaculum remains poorly characterized. In this study, a Gram-stain-negative bacterium, Tenacibaculum sp. SM2510, was isolated from seawater collected from Kongsfjorden, Svalbard, Norway. Genome sequencing revealed that the strain possesses a single circular chromosome of 2,904,982 bp with a G + C content of 31.44%, encoding 2564 protein-coding genes. Genomic analysis indicates that Tenacibaculum sp. SM2510 may directly take up extracellular oxidized glutathione (GSSG) and reduce it to reduced glutathione (GSH) through a reductive pathway, which potentially allows the strain to alleviate the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) caused by strong ultraviolet radiation and low temperature in polar environments. Furthermore, genomic analysis predicts that the strain degrades GSH to produce essential life-sustaining substances. In conclusion, these results suggest that Tenacibaculum sp. SM2510 may potentially utilize exogenous glutathione for both antioxidant defense and nutrient acquisition through direct GSH degradation, providing new insights into the environmental adaptive evolution of polar marine bacteria.

studies.title: Stability of glutathione added as a supplement to parenteral nutrition.
studies.abstract: Most very premature newborns (<32 weeks of gestation) receive parenteral nutrition (PN) that is inherently contaminated with peroxides. Oxidative stress induced by PN is associated with bronchopulmonary dysplasia, a main pathological complication in these infants who have weak antioxidant capacity to detoxify peroxides because of their glutathione deficiency. In animals, glutathione supplementation of PN prevented oxidative stress and alveolar loss (the main characteristic of bronchopulmonary dysplasia). Of its two forms-oxidized glutathione (GSSG) and reduced glutathione (GSH)-GSSG was used because of its better stability. However, a 30% loss of GSSG in PN is observed. The potentially high therapeutic benefits of GSSG supplementation on the health of very premature infants make the study of its stability highly important. GSSG was incubated in combination with the following components of PN: dextrose, multivitamins, Primene, and Travasol, and with cysteine, cystine, and peroxides, for 24 h. Total glutathione in these solutions was measured 0-24 h after the addition of GSSG. The combination of cysteine and multivitamins caused the maximum loss of glutathione. The stability of GSSG was not affected by multivitamins. The cysteine was responsible for ∼20% of the loss of GSSG; in the presence of multivitamins, the loss reached >70%. Removing the cysteine prevented the degradation of glutathione. GSSG reacts with cysteine to form cysteine-glutathione mixed disulfide, another suitable glutathione substrate for preterm neonates. The study confirms that GSSG added to PN can potentially provide a precursor to de novo synthesis of glutathione in vivo.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A small antioxidant molecule your cells make naturally; taken as a supplement to boost levels.
explanation.what_it_is: Glutathione is a tripeptide—a tiny protein made of three amino acids (glutamate, cysteine, and glycine) linked together. Your cells produce it constantly to neutralize harmful free radicals and support detoxification. It is water-loving (highly polar, XLogP −4.5), so it does not cross cell membranes easily on its own. People take it as an oral supplement, intravenous injection, or liposomal form (a fat-wrapped package designed to improve absorption).
explanation.how_it_works_line: Neutralizes damaging free radicals and resets redox enzymes that control inflammation and cell stress.
explanation.how_it_works: Glutathione works as a cellular antioxidant—it donates electrons to free radicals (unstable, reactive molecules) and disarms them before they damage proteins, DNA, or cell membranes. It also works as a cofactor (a helper molecule) for antioxidant enzymes like glutathione peroxidase and glutathione S-transferases, which break down toxins and peroxides. By reducing oxidative stress and rebalancing the cell's redox state (the ratio of oxidizing vs. reducing molecules), it can blunt inflammatory signaling pathways. Because it is highly polar and does not easily cross cell membranes, oral glutathione absorption in humans remains incompletely characterized—absorption varies dramatically by formulation, and some research questions whether oral doses substantially raise intracellular glutathione levels in all tissues.
explanation.safety_line: Mild side effects reported in small trials; long-term safety and drug interactions remain unstudied.
explanation.safety_detail: Retrieved trials reported glutathione supplementation as generally well-tolerated, with rare gastrointestinal side effects in short-term dosing (weeks to a few months). However, most published studies enrolled small numbers of healthy or mildly diseased adults for limited durations. Long-term safety—especially at higher or repeated doses, and in vulnerable populations—has not been adequately characterized in the records retrieved.
safety_bullets: Drug interactions: no interaction studies retrieved; potential effects with medications that depend on glutathione metabolism are untested.
Pregnancy and nursing: excluded from trials retrieved; safety unknown.
Kidney or liver disease: not systematically studied; patients with these conditions were largely excluded from available trials.
Intravenous or injectable forms: carry infection risk and require medical supervision; oral and liposomal forms have not been directly compared for safety.
explanation.chem_meaning: Glutathione's very negative lipophilicity (XLogP −4.5) means it is highly water-soluble but poorly lipid-soluble, making it difficult to cross fatty cell membranes without specialized transporters or formulation tricks (liposomes, NAC co-supplementation). This chemistry explains why oral glutathione bioavailability has long been questioned and why absorption depends heavily on delivery form.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four animal studies (2019–2024) showed that glutathione or liposomal glutathione supplementation reduced liver injury markers in rodent models of toxin-induced damage (diethylnitrosamine, lipopolysaccharide, tuberculosis), preserved protein synthesis, and enhanced antioxidant enzyme activity. No human trials on liver health were retrieved.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: All evidence is from animal models, which do not reliably predict human efficacy. No human trials exist in the records provided, so liver benefits remain hypothetical in people.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two small human RCTs tested oral glutathione in type 2 diabetes and obesity: one 3-week trial (n=10) in obese males examined insulin sensitivity; a second 2023 RCT in type 2 diabetics measured effects on gut microbiome composition. One rodent study examined l-cysteine and vitamin D co-supplementation in a musculoskeletal model. Human sample sizes are very small (~10 verified participants in the measured trial), and only one study directly measured glucose or insulin outcomes.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only two human studies with minimal verified sample size and imprecise reporting. Results have not been independently replicated. Animal data exist but do not substitute for human evidence on metabolic control.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: One human RCT (2023) in type 2 diabetics measured changes in gut microbiome after long-term oral glutathione supplementation. Three animal studies (2018–2023) showed that dietary glutathione supplementation improved intestinal barrier function, reduced oxidative stress markers, and enhanced disease resistance in treated fish and chemically injured rodent models. Sample sizes in the human trial could not be verified from abstracts.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only a single human study addresses this outcome, with unconfirmed sample size and no independent human replication. Consistency across human trials cannot be assessed. Animal data are suggestive but do not confirm effects in people.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seven human trials and one systematic review (n=194 verified across 2 studies; total sample estimated >204 but most studies omit sizes) investigated oral, intravenous, or liposomal glutathione in type 2 diabetes, obesity, endothelial dysfunction, and asthma (2015–2026). A 2026 systematic review summarized molecular mechanisms and skin aging; a 2023 RCT reported that combined citrulline and glutathione improved blood pressure and endothelial function; a 2015 RCT found oral glutathione supplementation increased body stores of the molecule. Twelve animal studies showed reduced inflammatory markers and oxidative stress in various disease models. A 2026 study in severe asthma linked glutathione metabolism to mitochondrial dysfunction.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple human trials exist, but most do not report sample sizes in abstracts, so total verified sample is small (~204 across 2 studies with stated n). One systematic review was identified but its findings have not been independently verified in other reviews. Consistency across trials is not fully established. Animal evidence is abundant and supportive, but human data remain modest in rigor and completeness.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base is mixed: inflammation has 7 human trials and a systematic review (Moderate grade), while blood sugar, gut health, and liver health rely on 2, 1, and 0 human RCTs respectively (Emerging to Preliminary). Human studies are mostly small and of recent vintage (2015–2026), with inconsistent reporting of sample size and outcome detail. Animal models are numerous (12–16 per outcome) and show consistent benefits for antioxidant activity and inflammatory markers, but animal data alone do not establish clinical efficacy in humans. The retrieved records represent a sample (~40 abstracts per outcome) and do not capture the entire literature.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records do not establish optimal glutathione dose, duration, or formulation (oral vs. liposomal vs. intravenous) for any outcome in humans. Whether oral glutathione substantially raises intracellular glutathione in tissues beyond the gut remains unclear. No trials comparing formulations head-to-head, no long-term safety data (>6 months), and no studies in children, pregnancy, or advanced kidney/liver disease were found. Most human trials enrolled small numbers of healthy or mildly diseased adults; whether benefits extend to severe or chronic disease states is untested.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base is dominated by animal studies and tiny human trials (median n=10 for blood sugar, only 1 human study for gut outcomes); no pooled effect sizes are available, making it impossible to assess true effect magnitude or consistency.

concerns.detail: All four liver health studies are animal models (2019–2024). The engine itself flags this as 'Indirectness: evidence is animal-only; does not reliably translate to humans.' Hepatoprotection in rodents or in vitro systems does not establish clinical benefit in human liver disease, and animal dose-response relationships often do not scale to human pharmacokinetics.

concerns.issue: Critically underpowered human trials for blood sugar
concerns.detail: Only 1 of 3 blood sugar studies reports sample size (n=10). The median across reported studies is 10 participants. With this sample size, clinically meaningful differences in insulin sensitivity or glycemic control cannot be reliably detected; a single outlier or publication bias can flip conclusions. Two human RCTs remain unverified for n and precision.

concerns.issue: Single human study isolated for gut/digestion outcomes
concerns.detail: One RCT addresses gut outcomes in humans (2023, microbiome study); three animal studies provide no replication. The engine notes 'Inconsistency: only one human study addresses this outcome; consistency cannot be assessed across independent human evidence.' A single small human study cannot support a robust claim about digestive benefit.

concerns.issue: Sample sizes mostly unreported across inflammation studies
concerns.detail: Inflammation is graded 'Moderate' based on 19 studies, but only 2 of 19 report sample size (n=10 and n=194). The median appears to be inflated by one large systematic review; the actual human trial evidence is opaque. Without visibility into sample sizes for ~17 of 19 studies, precision and risk of bias cannot be assessed.

concerns.issue: No pooled effect sizes reported for any outcome
concerns.detail: Across all four outcomes (liver, blood sugar, gut, inflammation), the records state 'pooled effect: none extractable.' This means no meta-analysis with a summary estimate and confidence interval is available. Claims about 'Moderate' or 'Preliminary' grades rest on narrative assessment of heterogeneous designs (RCT, animal, in vitro, unclassified), not quantitative synthesis.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The proposed mechanism (glutathione as antioxidant → reduced oxidative stress → improved liver/glycemic/inflammatory outcomes) is biologically plausible in isolated tissues and animal models. However, there is a large inferential leap between in vitro antioxidant activity and human clinical outcomes: systemic glutathione bioavailability is poor (most oral glutathione is degraded in the gut), cellular uptake is tightly regulated, and human trials have not convincingly shown that supplementation raises intracellular glutathione or translates to measurable clinical improvement in the outcomes claimed.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that the evidence is almost entirely animal and/or mechanistic: liver benefit exists only in animal models; blood sugar improvement has been tested in one n=10 human trial; and gut effects rest on a single human microbiome study. Oral glutathione has well-documented bioavailability problems, and no human trial has demonstrated clinically meaningful improvement in any of the four outcomes. The grades 'Moderate' and 'Preliminary' appear to reflect biological plausibility and animal efficacy, not demonstrated human benefit.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Well-powered (n≥100–150 per arm), adequately blinded RCTs in humans with pre-specified, clinically meaningful endpoints (e.g., HbA1c reduction ≥0.5%, ALT/AST normalization, CRP or TNF-α reduction) and biomarker confirmation of raised intracellular glutathione. Consistency across multiple independent human trials in the same outcome would also upgrade confidence substantially.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una pequeña molécula antioxidante que tus células producen naturalmente; se toma como suplemento para aumentar los niveles.
explanation_es.what_it_is: El glutatión es un tripéptido—una proteína diminuta hecha de tres aminoácidos (glutamato, cisteína y glicina) unidos entre sí. Tus células lo producen constantemente para neutralizar radicales libres dañinos y apoyar la desintoxicación. Es hidrofílico (altamente polar, XLogP −4.5), por lo que no cruza las membranas celulares fácilmente por sí solo. Las personas lo toman como suplemento oral, inyección intravenosa, o en forma liposomal (un paquete envuelto en grasa diseñado para mejorar la absorción).
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Neutraliza radicales libres dañinos y reinicia enzimas redox que controlan la inflamación y el estrés celular.
explanation_es.how_it_works: El glutatión actúa como antioxidante celular—dona electrones a radicales libres (moléculas inestables y reactivas) y los desactiva antes de que dañen proteínas, ADN o membranas celulares. También funciona como cofactor (una molécula auxiliar) para enzimas antioxidantes como la glutatión peroxidasa y las glutatión S-transferasas, que descomponen toxinas y peróxidos. Al reducir el estrés oxidativo y reequilibrar el estado redox de la célula (la proporción de moléculas oxidantes versus reductoras), puede atenuar las vías de señalización inflamatoria. Porque es altamente polar y no cruza fácilmente las membranas celulares, la absorción del glutatión oral en humanos sigue siendo incompleta—la absorción varía dramáticamente según la formulación, y algunas investigaciones cuestionan si las dosis orales aumentan sustancialmente los niveles de glutatión intracelular en todos los tejidos.
explanation_es.safety_line: Efectos secundarios leves reportados en ensayos pequeños; la seguridad a largo plazo y las interacciones farmacológicas siguen sin estudiarse.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos recuperados reportaron que la suplementación con glutatión fue generalmente bien tolerada, con efectos secundarios gastrointestinales raros en dosificación a corto plazo (semanas a algunos meses). Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estudios publicados incluyeron números pequeños de adultos sanos o levemente enfermos durante duraciones limitadas. La seguridad a largo plazo—especialmente a dosis más altas o repetidas, y en poblaciones vulnerables—no ha sido adecuadamente caracterizada en los registros recuperados.
safety_bullets: Interacciones farmacológicas: no se recuperaron estudios de interacción; los efectos potenciales con medicamentos que dependen del metabolismo del glutatión no han sido probados.
Embarazo y lactancia: excluidos de los ensayos recuperados; seguridad desconocida.
Enfermedad renal o hepática: no estudiado sistemáticamente; los pacientes con estas condiciones fueron mayormente excluidos de los ensayos disponibles.
Formas intravenosas o inyectables: conllevan riesgo de infección y requieren supervisión médica; las formas oral y liposomal no han sido comparadas directamente en cuanto a seguridad.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La lipofilicidad muy negativa del glutatión (XLogP −4.5) significa que es altamente soluble en agua pero poco soluble en lípidos, lo que dificulta cruzar membranas celulares grasas sin transportadores especializados o trucos de formulación (liposomas, cosuplantación con NAC). Esta química explica por qué la biodisponibilidad del glutatión oral ha sido cuestionada durante mucho tiempo y por qué la absorción depende fuertemente de la forma de administración.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro estudios en animales (2019–2024) mostraron que la suplementación con glutatión o glutatión liposomal redujo los marcadores de lesión hepática en modelos de roedores de daño inducido por toxinas (dietilnitrosamina, lipopolisacárido, tuberculosis), preservó la síntesis de proteínas y mejoró la actividad de enzimas antioxidantes. No se recuperaron ensayos humanos sobre salud hepática.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Toda la evidencia proviene de modelos en animales, que no predicen de manera confiable la eficacia en humanos. No existen ensayos humanos en los registros proporcionados, por lo que los beneficios hepáticos siguen siendo hipotéticos en personas.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos pequeños ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos probaron glutatión oral en diabetes tipo 2 y obesidad: un ensayo de 3 semanas (n=10) en hombres obesos examinó la sensibilidad a la insulina; un segundo ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2023 en diabéticos tipo 2 midió efectos en la composición del microbioma intestinal. Un estudio en roedores examinó la cosuplantación de l-cisteína y vitamina D en un modelo musculoesquelético. Los tamaños de muestra humana son muy pequeños (~10 participantes verificados en el ensayo medido), y solo un estudio midió directamente glucosa o resultados de insulina.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo dos estudios humanos con tamaño de muestra verificado muy pequeño y reporte impreciso. Los resultados no han sido replicados de forma independiente. Los datos en animales existen pero no sustituyen la evidencia humana sobre control metabólico.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado humano (2023) en diabéticos tipo 2 midió cambios en el microbioma intestinal después de suplementación oral a largo plazo con glutatión. Tres estudios en animales (2018–2023) mostraron que la suplementación dietética con glutatión mejoró la función de barrera intestinal, redujo marcadores de estrés oxidativo y mejoró la resistencia a enfermedades en peces tratados y modelos de roedores con lesión química. Los tamaños de muestra en el ensayo humano no pudieron ser verificados a partir de resúmenes.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo un único estudio humano aborda este resultado, con tamaño de muestra no confirmado y sin replicación humana independiente. La consistencia entre ensayos humanos no puede ser evaluada. Los datos en animales son sugestivos pero no confirman efectos en personas.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Siete ensayos humanos y una revisión sistemática (n=194 verificados en 2 estudios; muestra total estimada >204 pero la mayoría de los estudios omiten tamaños) investigaron glutatión oral, intravenoso o liposomal en diabetes tipo 2, obesidad, disfunción endotelial y asma (2015–2026). Una revisión sistemática de 2026 resumió mecanismos moleculares y envejecimiento de la piel; un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2023 reportó que citrulina combinada y glutatión mejoraron la presión arterial y la función endotelial; un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2015 encontró que la suplementación oral con glutatión aumentó los depósitos corporales de la molécula. Doce estudios en animales mostraron marcadores inflamatorios reducidos y estrés oxidativo en varios modelos de enfermedad. Un estudio de 2026 en asma grave vinculó el metabolismo del glutatión con disfunción mitocondrial.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Existen múltiples ensayos humanos, pero la mayoría no reporta tamaños de muestra en resúmenes, por lo que la muestra total verificada es pequeña (~204 en 2 estudios con n declarado). Se identificó una revisión sistemática pero sus hallazgos no han sido verificados de forma independiente en otras revisiones. La consistencia entre ensayos no está completamente establecida. La evidencia en animales es abundante y favorable, pero los datos humanos siguen siendo modestos en rigor e integridad.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia es mixta: la inflamación tiene 7 ensayos humanos y una revisión sistemática (grado Moderada), mientras que azúcar en sangre, salud intestinal y salud hepática se basan en 2, 1 y 0 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados humanos respectivamente (Emergente a Preliminar). Los estudios humanos son mayormente pequeños y de reciente creación (2015–2026), con reporte inconsistente del tamaño de muestra y detalle de resultado. Los modelos en animales son numerosos (12–16 por resultado) y muestran beneficios consistentes para actividad antioxidante y marcadores inflamatorios, pero los datos en animales por sí solos no establecen eficacia clínica en humanos. Los registros recuperados representan una muestra (~40 resúmenes por resultado) y no capturan la literatura completa.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados no establecen la dosis óptima, duración o formulación de glutatión (oral versus liposomal versus intravenosa) para ningún resultado en humanos. Si el glutatión oral aumenta sustancialmente el glutatión intracelular en tejidos más allá del intestino sigue siendo poco claro. No hay ensayos comparando formulaciones frente a frente, sin datos de seguridad a largo plazo (>6 meses), y sin estudios en niños, embarazo o enfermedad renal/hepática avanzada. La mayoría de los ensayos humanos incluyeron números pequeños de adultos sanos o levemente enfermos; si los beneficios se extienden a estados de enfermedad grave o crónica no ha sido probado.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia está dominada por estudios en animales y ensayos humanos muy pequeños (mediana n=10 para azúcar en sangre, solo 1 estudio humano para resultados intestinales); no hay estimaciones de efectos agrupadas disponibles, lo que hace imposible evaluar la verdadera magnitud del efecto o la consistencia.

concerns.issue: Evidencia solo en animales para la salud hepática
concerns.detail: Los cuatro estudios de salud hepática son modelos animales (2019–2024). El motor mismo lo señala como 'Indirectitud: la evidencia es solo en animales; no se traduce de manera confiable a humanos.' La hepatoprotección en roedores o sistemas in vitro no establece beneficio clínico en enfermedades hepáticas humanas, y las relaciones dosis-respuesta en animales a menudo no se escalan a la farmacocinética humana.

concerns.issue: Ensayos humanos críticamente insuficientemente potenciados para azúcar en sangre
concerns.detail: Solo 1 de 3 estudios de azúcar en sangre reporta tamaño de muestra (n=10). La mediana entre los estudios reportados es de 10 participantes. Con este tamaño de muestra, las diferencias clínicamente significativas en la sensibilidad a la insulina o el control glucémico no pueden detectarse de manera confiable; un único valor atípico o sesgo de publicación puede invertir las conclusiones. Dos ensayos clínicos aleatorizados humanos permanecen sin verificar para n y precisión.

concerns.issue: Estudio humano único y aislado para resultados intestinales/digestivos
concerns.detail: Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado aborda resultados intestinales en humanos (2023, estudio del microbioma); tres estudios en animales no proporcionan replicación. El motor señala 'Inconsistencia: solo un estudio humano aborda este resultado; la consistencia no puede evaluarse en la evidencia humana independiente.' Un único estudio humano pequeño no puede respaldar una afirmación sólida sobre beneficio digestivo.

concerns.issue: Tamaños de muestra mayormente no reportados en estudios de inflamación
concerns.detail: La inflamación se califica como 'Moderada' basada en 19 estudios, pero solo 2 de 19 reportan tamaño de muestra (n=10 y n=194). La mediana parece estar inflada por una revisión sistemática grande; la evidencia real del ensayo humano es opaca. Sin visibilidad del tamaño de muestra para aproximadamente 17 de 19 estudios, la precisión y el riesgo de sesgo no pueden evaluarse.

concerns.issue: Sin estimaciones de efectos agrupadas reportadas para ningún resultado
concerns.detail: En los cuatro resultados (hígado, azúcar en sangre, intestino, inflamación), los registros establecen 'efecto agrupado: ninguno extraíble.' Esto significa que no hay metanálisis con una estimación de resumen e intervalo de confianza disponible. Las afirmaciones sobre calificaciones 'Moderada' o 'Preliminar' se basan en evaluación narrativa de diseños heterogéneos (ensayo clínico aleatorizado, animal, in vitro, sin clasificar), no en síntesis cuantitativa.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El mecanismo propuesto (glutatión como antioxidante → estrés oxidativo reducido → resultados hepáticos/glucémicos/inflamatorios mejorados) es biológicamente plausible en tejidos aislados y modelos animales. Sin embargo, hay un gran salto inferencial entre la actividad antioxidante in vitro y los resultados clínicos humanos: la biodisponibilidad sistémica del glutatión es pobre (la mayoría del glutatión oral se degrada en el intestino), la captación celular está estrictamente regulada, y los ensayos humanos no han demostrado de manera convincente que la suplementación aumente el glutatión intracelular o se traduzca en mejora clínica medible en los resultados afirmados.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que la evidencia es casi completamente en animales y/o mecanística: el beneficio hepático existe solo en modelos animales; la mejora del azúcar en sangre se ha probado en un ensayo humano con n=10; y los efectos intestinales descansan en un único estudio del microbioma humano. El glutatión oral tiene problemas bien documentados de biodisponibilidad, y ningún ensayo humano ha demostrado mejora clínicamente significativa en ninguno de los cuatro resultados. Las calificaciones 'Moderada' y 'Preliminar' parecen reflejar plausibilidad biológica y eficacia en animales, no beneficio humano demostrado.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Ensayos clínicos aleatorizados bien potenciados (n≥100–150 por brazo) en humanos, adecuadamente ciegos con puntos finales prespecificados y clínicamente significativos (p. ej., reducción de HbA1c ≥0.5%, normalización de ALT/AST, reducción de CRP o TNF-α) y confirmación de biomarcadores de glutatión intracelular elevado. La consistencia en múltiples ensayos humanos independientes en el mismo resultado también mejoraría sustancialmente la confianza.
